workarounds.symptom: [Bug]: Kubernetes runs keep failing after the jump pod is evicted
workarounds.workaround: Fix: Kubernetes: manage the jump pod with a ReplicaSet. Target files: src/dstack/_internal/core/backends/kubernetes/compute.py, src/dstack/_internal/core/backends/kubernetes/resources.py, src/dstack/_internal/core/backends/kubernetes/utils.py. The jump pod was a bare pod, reused for as long as it existed. Once evicted, for example due to node pressure, it stayed in the Failed phase and was never recreated, so every job in the project failed until someone deleted the pod by hand. (Ref: https://github.com/dstackai/dstack/pull/4447)
Fix: Fix unit tests with older `azure-mgmt-compute`. Applied modifications to pyproject.toml. (Ref: https://github.com/dstackai/dstack/pull/4435)
Fix: Fix unit tests with older `openai`. Applied modifications to pyproject.toml. (Ref: https://github.com/dstackai/dstack/pull/4437)

workarounds.symptom: [Bug]: Kubernetes: job pod gets stuck in a restart loop
workarounds.workaround: Fix: Scope runner pull, metrics and stop to the job submission. Target files: runner/internal/runner/api/http.go, runner/internal/runner/api/server.go, runner/internal/runner/api/server_test.go. The server could not tell the runner it submitted a job to from another one at the same address. A container restarted by the backend (e.g., Kubernetes' default `restartPolicy: Always`) answers /api/pull with no job states, which the server took for a healthy running job, while the new runner waited for a submission that never came, exite... (Ref: https://github.com/dstackai/dstack/pull/4425)
